# DPO Pay — build spec

The eight items requested before production code. Architecture approved
2026-09-13; decisions from that approval are recorded here as **DECIDED** and
are not reopened.

Companion documents:
- `docs/UGANDA-DPO-PAY-INTEGRATION-PLAN.md` — the architecture assessment
- `migrations/071_dpo_payments.sql` — item 3, written and validated
- `tools/dpo_payment_method.php` — resolves item 1 against the live uCRM

---

## 1. The DPO Pay payment-method UUID

**Not yet obtainable from here, and not inventable.** The UUID is generated by
uCRM when the method is created. This session has no route to
`crm.dishnetuganda.com` — uCRM is reachable only from the server. So instead of
guessing a value, `tools/dpo_payment_method.php` obtains it there:

```
docker exec -it ucrm php /data/ucrm/data/plugins/dishnet-hybrid-sudan/tools/dpo_payment_method.php --store
```

It lists every payment method on the instance with its UUID, finds a DPO one,
and if none exists **asks uCRM to create it** — then reports verbatim what uCRM
answered.

**Settled on the live instance, 2026-09-13:** uCRM **does** accept
`POST /payment-methods`. The tool created `DPO Pay` against
`http://localhost/crm/api/v2.1` on an instance that already held 21 methods
(Cash, Bank transfer, Eco Bank UGX/USD, and the built-in gateway entries), and
returned its UUID. This was genuinely unknown before — the API could equally
have been read-only — so it is recorded here rather than assumed for the next
install.

If a future instance does refuse, the tool prints the refusal and the manual
path:

> uCRM → System → Billing → Payment methods → Add → name `DPO Pay`

then `--store` again to vault the UUID as `dpo_payment_method_uuid`.

**Nothing downstream hardcodes it.** The service reads it from the vault at
settle time and **refuses to post a payment if it is unset** — which is what
stops a DPO payment silently falling back to Cash and entering agent cash
reconciliation.

---

## 2. The exact uCRM request that records the payment

Built only after `verifyToken` returned `000` and the amount, currency and
CompanyRef all matched the stored row.

```php
$payload = [
    'clientId'     => (int)$row['crm_client_id'],
    'methodId'     => $dpoMethodUuid,          // vault; empty ⇒ refuse, never Cash
    'amount'       => (float)$row['amount'],   // the stored figure, not DPO's echo
    'currencyCode' => dn_payload_currency($row['currency'], $config),
    'note'         => "DPO Pay | Ref: {$row['reference']}"
                    . " | DPO TransRef: {$row['dpo_trans_ref']}"
                    . " | Invoice: {$row['invoice_number']}"
                    . " | Env: {$row['environment']}",
    'applyToInvoicesAutomatically' => true,
];
$result = $crm->createPaymentSafe($payload, $row['reference']);
```

Three deliberate choices:

- **`applyToInvoicesAutomatically`** — uCRM settles the invoice. We never PATCH
  an invoice status. This is the distinction that keeps the finance audit trail
  honest.
- **`amount` comes from our row**, not from DPO's verify response. DPO's figure
  is used to *check* ours; if they disagree the payment does not post at all.
- **`reference` as the unique ref**, so `createPaymentSafe`'s own duplicate scan
  has something exact to match — behind our unique index, not instead of it.

**On failure** the row goes to `PENDING` with `failure_reason` set and the
existing `crm_payment_retry.json` queue takes it, exactly as the field-agent
path already does. Money received is never dropped because uCRM was briefly
unreachable.

## 3. The migration

`migrations/071_dpo_payments.sql` — written, applied to a scratch database, and
its guarantees exercised. Verified behaviour:

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| Same `reference` twice | refused — `UNIQUE constraint failed: dpo_payments.reference` |
| A second OPEN attempt on the same invoice | refused — `UNIQUE constraint failed: dpo_payments.crm_invoice_id` |
| A new attempt after the previous one EXPIRED | **allowed** — this is the retry path |
| Two DPO payments claiming one uCRM payment | refused — `UNIQUE constraint failed: dpo_payments.crm_payment_id` |
| Editing an attempt's amount or currency | refused — *fixed at creation* |
| Moving an attempt between test and live | refused — *fixed at creation* |
| Un-settling a settled payment | refused — *refund it* |
| `SUCCESS → REFUNDED` | **allowed** |
| Deleting a payment or an event | refused |
| Editing payment history | refused |

Two columns exist because of the approved decisions:

- **`QUARANTINED`** in the status set — decision 3 (no partial payments): when
  the verified amount is not the full outstanding, or the figures disagree with
  ours, money has moved but this is not a clean settlement. Nothing posts to
  uCRM; a person decides.
- **`attempt_expires_at`** — decision 5 (30-minute attempt). This is *our*
  expiry. DPO's `PTL` is advisory, and DPO's own modules never send it (see
  item 4), so an attempt's expiry cannot depend on a remote system honouring a
  hint.

---

## 4. The exact DPO XML

### createToken — `POST https://secure.3gdirectpay.com/API/v6/`

Body, no auth header, `cache-control: no-cache`:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<API3G>
  <CompanyToken>{vault: dpo_company_token}</CompanyToken>
  <Request>createToken</Request>
  <Transaction>
    <PaymentAmount>299000.00</PaymentAmount>
    <PaymentCurrency>UGX</PaymentCurrency>
    <CompanyRef>DPO-125-7-K3M9QX</CompanyRef>
    <customerFirstName>Grace</customerFirstName>
    <customerLastName>Nakato</customerLastName>
    <customerEmail>grace@example.com</customerEmail>
    <customerPhone>256772000000</customerPhone>
    <customerDialCode>256</customerDialCode>
    <customerCountry>UG</customerCountry>
    <customerCity></customerCity>
    <customerAddress></customerAddress>
    <customerZip></customerZip>
    <RedirectURL>https://crm.dishnetuganda.com/crm/_plugins/dishnet-hybrid-sudan/public.php?page=dpo_return</RedirectURL>
    <BackURL>https://crm.dishnetuganda.com/crm/_plugins/dishnet-hybrid-sudan/public.php?page=dpo_return&amp;cancelled=1</BackURL>
    <CompanyAccRef>{vault: dpo_company_acc_ref}</CompanyAccRef>
    <PTL>30</PTL>
    <PTLtype>minutes</PTLtype>
  </Transaction>
  <Services>
    <Service>
      <ServiceType>{vault: dpo_service_type}</ServiceType>
      <ServiceDescription>DishNet Home - Monthly Internet Service (INV-2026-00125)</ServiceDescription>
      <ServiceDate>2026/09/13 14:22</ServiceDate>
    </Service>
  </Services>
</API3G>
```

Notes on specific fields:

- **`customerPhone`** is digits only. DPO's own class strips non-digits with
  `preg_replace('/\D/','')`; we do the same before sending rather than relying
  on it.
- **URLs are built from `dn_plugin_public($config)`**, never hardcoded — that
  helper is already the one source of truth for this install's public address,
  with its documented override for when uCRM reports an internally-correct but
  externally-wrong hostname.
- **There is no `NotifyURL` field.** The push URL is not part of createToken, so
  it must be registered with DPO out of band. **UNCONFIRMED — for DPO.**
- **`PTL` / `PTLtype`** — `PTLtype: minutes` comes from DPO's API documentation
  as surfaced in search; I could not open the page from here.
  **Treat the spelling as unconfirmed.** Both values are config, and the field
  pair is omitted entirely when unset. Worth knowing: **DPO's own WooCommerce
  module never sends PTL at all** — only their common class supports it. This
  is exactly why `attempt_expires_at` exists on our side.
- Every value is XML-escaped before interpolation. DPO's own class interpolates
  raw, which would break on an ampersand in a customer's name; ours will not.

### verifyToken — `POST https://secure.3gdirectpay.com/API/v7/`

Note the version change. This is not a typo: DPO's current common class posts
createToken to v6 and verifyToken to v7.

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<API3G>
  <CompanyToken>{vault: dpo_company_token}</CompanyToken>
  <Request>verifyToken</Request>
  <TransactionToken>1B2E3F4A-…</TransactionToken>
</API3G>
```

Expected success shape:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<API3G>
  <Result>000</Result>
  <ResultExplanation>Transaction Paid</ResultExplanation>
  <CompanyRef>DPO-125-7-K3M9QX</CompanyRef>
  <TransactionApproval>…</TransactionApproval>
  <TransactionCurrency>UGX</TransactionCurrency>
  <TransactionAmount>299000.00</TransactionAmount>
  <CustomerName>…</CustomerName>
  <CustomerCreditType>…</CustomerCreditType>
</API3G>
```

**Field names in the verify response beyond `Result`, `ResultExplanation`,
`CompanyRef` and `CustomerCreditType` are UNCONFIRMED** — those four are the
ones DPO's own plugin reads. The client will parse defensively: a missing
amount or currency element means *we could not confirm the figures*, which
quarantines rather than settles. It never means *assume they match*.

## 5. State transitions

```
                        ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
                        │  Pay Now  (feature flag must be ON)      │
                        └────────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
                                             │ live invoice re-read
                                             │ ownership + payable checks
                                             ▼
                                        ┌─────────┐
                                        │ CREATED │  row written, no DPO call yet
                                        └────┬────┘
                        createToken          │
            ┌────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┐
            │ Result 000                     │ 940 already paid           │ 8xx/9xx
            ▼                                ▼                            ▼
      ┌──────────┐                    ┌─────────────┐              ┌────────┐
      │ PENDING  │                    │ reconcile,  │              │ FAILED │
      └────┬─────┘                    │ never re-   │              └────────┘
           │ customer sent to DPO     │ charge      │
           ▼                          └─────────────┘
    ┌─────────────┐
    │ REDIRECTED  │◄──── the only state the customer is "at DPO" in
    └──────┬──────┘
           │
           │  return · push · cron  →  ALL call verifyAndSettle()
           │
   ┌───────┼─────────┬──────────┬──────────┬─────────────┐
   │ 000   │ 001/900 │ 901      │ 903      │ 904         │ amount ≠ ours
   │ AND   │         │          │          │             │ or 002
   │ all   ▼         ▼          ▼          ▼             ▼
   │ checks│    ┌─────────┐ ┌────────┐ ┌─────────┐ ┌──────────────┐
   │ pass  │    │ PENDING │ │ FAILED │ │ EXPIRED │ │ QUARANTINED  │
   │       │    └────┬────┘ └────────┘ └─────────┘ └──────────────┘
   ▼       │         │ still open          │            no uCRM payment,
┌─────────┐│         │ → cron retries      │            a person decides
│ SUCCESS ││         │                     │
└────┬────┘│         └── attempt_expires_at passed ──► EXPIRED
     │     │
     │     └── our own expiry runs even if DPO never answers
     ▼
┌──────────┐
│ REFUNDED │   admin-recorded only; DPO's refund mechanism is UNCONFIRMED
└──────────┘
```

Rules the diagram encodes:

- `CREATED`, `PENDING` and `REDIRECTED` are the **open** states — the ones the
  partial unique index counts, so only one can exist per invoice at a time.
- `EXPIRED`, `FAILED` and `CANCELLED` are terminal for *that attempt*, not for
  the invoice. **Decision 5:** the customer may start a fresh attempt; the
  invoice does not expire.
- `SUCCESS` is reachable **only** from `verifyAndSettle()` after a `000` whose
  CompanyRef, amount and currency all match the stored row.
- `QUARANTINED` is a decision point, not a failure: money moved, but not as a
  clean full settlement. **Decision 3.**
- `SUCCESS → REFUNDED` is the only transition out of `SUCCESS`, enforced by
  trigger.

---

## 6. Endpoints

Following this application's routing, not the `/api/payments/dpo/*` shape from
the original brief.

| Route | Auth | Method | Does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `?page=api&action=dpo_initiate` | Bearer JWT (`ca_require_auth`) | POST | Takes **only** `invoice_id`. Re-reads the invoice live, checks ownership against the JWT claim, computes payable, creates or reuses the open attempt, calls createToken. Returns `{ checkout_url }` and nothing else. Refuses when the feature flag is off. |
| `?page=api&action=dpo_status` | Bearer JWT | GET | Takes `reference`. Returns the **stored** status of the caller's own attempt, for the pending screen to poll. Never triggers a charge. |
| `?page=dpo_return` | none (customer's browser) | GET | Reads `TransactionToken`, resolves it to a row, calls `verifyAndSettle()`, renders success / pending / failed **from the stored row**. Never from the query string. |
| `?page=dpo_push` | none (DPO's server) | POST | Reads `<API3G>` XML, takes only `CompanyRef`/`TransactionToken`, echoes `OK`, calls `verifyAndSettle()`. Rate-limited; unknown references logged and discarded. |
| Admin tab `dpo_payments` | `*admin` | GET | Reconciliation screen: filter by status, date, customer, invoice, reference, environment; row opens the event timeline. |

`dpo_push` echoes `OK` **before** verification, because DPO expects that
acknowledgement and a slow verify must not make them retry. The acknowledgement
says *received*; it says nothing about the outcome.

### Feature flag — `dpo_enabled`

Vault key, default **off**. When off:

- `dpo_initiate` refuses with a plain message and logs `disabled_by_flag`
- Pay Now is hidden in the portal
- `dpo_return`, `dpo_push` and the reconcile cron **keep working**, so
  transactions already in flight still settle

Nothing about existing invoices, payment methods, other payment paths or agent
cash reconciliation is touched by the flag in either position.

---

## 7. Reconciliation cron

`cron/dpo_reconcile.php`, registered in the `cron/master.php` interval table at
**300 seconds**. It is the third leg: the customer who paid on their phone and
closed the browser.

```
every 5 minutes:
  rows WHERE status IN ('CREATED','PENDING','REDIRECTED')       ← idx_dpo_open_age
    AND created_at < now - 2 minutes            ← let the return path go first
  oldest first, capped per run

  for each row:
    no dpo_trans_token?        → never reached DPO → FAILED, reason recorded
    attempt_expires_at passed
      AND verify says unpaid?  → EXPIRED   (our clock, not DPO's)
    otherwise                  → verifyAndSettle($row['reference'])

  never more than N verifies per run; a row that has been verified within the
  last minute is skipped, so a push and the cron cannot both hammer DPO for the
  same token
```

Behaviour that matters:

- It calls **the same** `verifyAndSettle()` as the other two channels. There is
  no second settlement path to keep in step.
- It is safe to run while `dpo_enabled` is off — disabling new payments must not
  strand money already taken.
- It `return;`s, never `exit()`s: `master.php` *includes* its crons, and an
  `exit()` would silently kill every cron scheduled after it.
- Expiry is decided by `attempt_expires_at` **and** a verify that says unpaid —
  never by the clock alone, because a payment completing at minute 29 must not
  be expired at minute 30.

## 8. Test matrix

Run against `tests/fixtures/fake_dpo_server.php`, as EFRIS and Evolution already
are. **The fake server is not skipped because a test merchant token exists** —
it is the only way to exercise result codes a real test account will rarely
produce, and it makes failures deterministic.

### Client — every documented result code

| # | Scenario | Expect |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | createToken `000` | token + ref captured, row → PENDING |
| 2 | createToken `801/802` (token missing/unknown) | FAILED, credential error surfaced to admin, never to the customer |
| 3 | createToken `904` currency not supported | FAILED, **no conversion attempted** |
| 4 | createToken `905/906` limits exceeded | FAILED, reason recorded |
| 5 | createToken `940` CompanyRef already paid | **never re-charge** — reconcile instead |
| 6 | Malformed XML / HTML error page back | FAILED, raw response truncated into the event, no crash |
| 7 | verifyToken `000` | settle path entered |
| 8 | verifyToken `001` Authorized | **stays PENDING** — authorized is not paid |
| 9 | verifyToken `002` over/underpaid | QUARANTINED, no uCRM payment |
| 10 | verifyToken `900` | PENDING |
| 11 | verifyToken `901` | FAILED |
| 12 | verifyToken `903` | EXPIRED |
| 13 | verifyToken `904` | CANCELLED |
| 14 | Connection timeout on verify | row unchanged, retried next cron — never FAILED on our own network fault |

### Service — the fourteen scenarios from the brief

| # | Scenario | Expect |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Successful card payment | one uCRM payment, invoice settled by uCRM |
| 2 | Successful MTN Mobile Money | identical path; method recorded as DPO reported it |
| 3 | Successful Airtel Money | identical path |
| 4 | Failed payment | FAILED, invoice untouched |
| 5 | Cancelled checkout | CANCELLED, invoice untouched |
| 6 | Pending payment | PENDING; customer screen never says successful |
| 7 | **Duplicate callback ×3** | exactly **one** uCRM payment; 2nd and 3rd are no-ops |
| 8 | Customer refreshes the return page ×5 | one payment; page re-renders from the stored row |
| 9 | **Pay Now clicked twice** | one attempt reused; no second token, no second charge |
| 10 | Invoice already fully paid | initiate refuses before calling DPO |
| 11 | Invoice partially paid elsewhere | payable = **live** outstanding, not the cached total |
| 12 | Expired / unknown reference at return | neutral "not completed" page; nothing settled |
| 13 | DPO times out at createToken | row FAILED, customer told plainly, invoice untouched |
| 14 | Verification API unavailable at settle | stays open; cron settles it later |

### Concurrency, money and safety

| # | Scenario | Expect |
|---|---|---|
| 15 | Push and return race on one token | one uCRM payment — proven at the index, not just the logic |
| 16 | Push and reconcile cron race | one uCRM payment |
| 17 | **Underpayment** (DPO reports less than outstanding) | QUARANTINED — decision 3 |
| 18 | Verified currency ≠ stored currency | QUARANTINED, no conversion |
| 19 | Verified CompanyRef ≠ our reference | settles nothing, alert raised |
| 20 | Forged push claiming `<Result>000</Result>` | **nothing settles** — we ask DPO, we do not read their claim |
| 21 | Payment succeeds but uCRM POST fails | row keeps the money's truth, retry queue drains it, still one payment |
| 22 | `dpo_payment_method_uuid` unset | **refuse to post** — never fall back to Cash |
| 23 | Feature flag off mid-flight | initiate refused; the in-flight attempt still settles |
| 24 | Test-environment row | excluded from revenue reporting, visibly marked |
| 25 | Another customer's invoice id in the request | 403, attempt audited |
| 26 | Amount supplied in the request body | ignored entirely — the server never reads it |

## Still blocking production activation

Unchanged and not to be invented. Framework building proceeds; **go-live does
not** until DPO confirms:

UGX availability · MTN Mobile Money · Airtel Money · test company token · live
company token · `ServiceType` · `CompanyAccRef` · push/callback registration
process · refund process · transaction limits · merchant onboarding
requirements · the `PTLtype` spelling.

Where DPO's current merchant onboarding gives account-specific instructions that
differ from the published code read here, **DPO's instructions win** and this
document is corrected.
